## Nivyx v2.3.1

A reliability release: installing, updating and uninstalling are now
safe to fail on every platform. No changes to how the DPI bypass works.

### Windows
- `dpi-proxy.exe` opened from Explorer now explains that it is the
  internal engine and what to open instead, and changes nothing.
  (Before, it silently started a plain SOCKS5 proxy that protected
  nothing.) From a terminal it behaves as before.
- `Install Nivyx.cmd` / `Uninstall Nivyx.cmd` report the real result and
  exit code, including a declined administrator prompt, a damaged
  package and being run from inside the ZIP.
- A failed upgrade puts the previous version back and starts it.
- Service start failures say why (e.g. a blocked or damaged driver).
- `nivyx update` works when started from a PowerShell 7 window.

### Linux
- A failed build or a missing dependency no longer stops a running
  Nivyx. A failed reinstall or migration restores the previous install,
  including installs from before v2.3, which keep their old names until
  the new service is healthy.
- A plain uninstall keeps settings and learned state; `--purge` removes
  them.
- The update package runs on glibc 2.35+ (Debian 12, Ubuntu 22.04 and
  newer). The v2.3.0 package needed glibc 2.38.
- arm64 is CI-tested (install from source).

### macOS
- A plain uninstall keeps settings, learned state and logs; `--purge`
  removes them. (Before, everything was removed every time.)
- A failed reinstall restores the previous installation. The launchers
  report the real exit code.
- The installer no longer strips the quarantine flag from the whole
  extracted folder.

### Everywhere
- `nivyx update` backs up every replaced file under a unique name,
  refuses packages with unexpected paths or links, keeps its backup if a
  rollback fails, and accepts the test override only for 127.0.0.1.
- `nivyx status` shows "Active" only for a live engine (matching process,
  fresh heartbeat).
- The SBOM states Nivyx's license and the real Windows OpenSSL version.

Upgrading in place from v2.1.0, v2.2.x and v2.3.0 works as before.
`nivyx update` in v2.2.x and v2.3.0 installs this release: the package
layout those updaters expect is unchanged.
